The intervention "Strengthening Civil Society Actors and Networks Advocating for a Just Environmental Transition in the Middle East and North Africa" aims at promoting capacities of CSOs to become competent and vocal actors in the climate action in the Mena region. The Sida co-financing is designed to be fully integrated into an EU (DG-NEAR) funded programme titled "Strengthening Civil Society Actors: Toward a Just Environmental Transition in the Middle East and North Africa". The Sida co-financing is scheduled for an implementation period for 2.5 years starting 1 June 2023 with a budget of 10 MSEK. The Sida funds will be utilised to cover the 10% cost share of the EU programme to specifically strengthen youth and feminist CSO networks, expand activities to additional countries namely, Algeria, Jordan, Iraq, Palestine and Yemen, and to support CSOs to follow, monitor and contribute to processes related international climate negotiations.

During the reporting period, the project successfully transitioned from regional expansion to full implementation across the five SIDA-funded countries: Algeria, Palestine, Jordan, Iraq, and Yemen. Building on the foundations established in Egypt, Lebanon, Tunisia, and Morocco, ARI strengthened partnerships and delivered concrete results in research, policy dialogue, and stakeholder engagement.
ARI facilitated consultations, roundtables, and policy discussions on energy transition, food sovereignty, and water justice, engaging participants from civil society, academia, youth groups, and policymaking institutions. Despite operating in diverse and often fragile contexts, the project sustained inclusive and meaningful stakeholder engagement across all target countries.
The project also advanced evidence-based advocacy through the production of country-specific research on energy, water, and food governance issues, providing locally grounded analysis to inform national and regional policy discussions.
At the regional level, ARI increased the visibility and impact of project findings through participation in the Yemen International Forum and the Sulaimani Forum, as well as by convening the regional conference Divergent Pathways to Energy Justice: Comparative Perspectives from MENA in December 2025. These engagements strengthened cross-country collaboration and positioned ARI and its partners as key contributors to just transition debates in the MENA region.
In addition, the Youth Organisations Training on Climate Action and Advocacy enhanced the capacities of youth-led organisations and created opportunities for meaningful participation in climate governance processes, including engagement at COP30.
